claims.statement: The harness normalizes Harlo RPC and Claude stream-json into a shared event vocabulary consumed by Qt-independent core logic.
SessionHandle queues controls, can open saved history without starting a harness, and gives subscribers snapshots before deltas; active stream flushing is batched at 100 ms.
ChatSession queues updates to the Qt thread and rejects old-binding updates using a generation counter, unsubscribing on rebind or drop.
Harlo's database stores application metadata separately from agent conversation files, and Harlo session discovery reads the head and tail of large JSONL files.
The demo session test checks lifecycle transitions and verifies that a late subscriber receives the same rows as the existing subscriber.
harlo-code draws code without Qt while the desktop CodeView presents the image and forwards user input.
Finished wiki sessions have a separately expandable Wiki shelf after Settled; workspace settlement defers active or unsaved sessions and respects disabling, pinning and archiving.
Markdown approval requests use rendered prose/code blocks in a bounded scrolling request body while non-Markdown requests retain plain text.

The session driver holds new-turn prompts during asynchronous undo snapshots, reports preparation to new subscribers, and on abort invalidates late completion and returns all held messages in send order with wire text, images, mode and optional original typed metadata.
Session metadata stores cost classification separately from numeric cost, and the session context report carries that classification as `costKind`.

Cancelled prompts restore sender-supplied typed words and attachment paths without recent-send matching; fallback strips plan/photo wrappers, desktop saves inline pictures when paths are absent, deduplicates attachments and prepends words above a newer draft.
Agent session searches execute off the UI thread before workspace metadata filtering; results exclude the caller and contain at most eight sessions and two passages per session.
Asynchronous desktop message searches check the latest generation after acquiring the search-reader lock, skipping obsolete queries still waiting to execute.

Transcript Markdown splits long code into 150-line pieces and tables into 100-row pieces, leaves the live final piece uncached, and retains complete code on the first continuation row for copying while ordinary rendering keeps whole blocks.

Local Harlo search reads continue from complete lines only when the saved tail and parent chain match; branch or rewrite changes trigger a full active-branch read, and the search index migrates a row-ID map to delete replaced or removed messages efficiently.

Unsent prompts from failed harness starts or cancelled preparation receive a transcript notice; with no composing sink attached, the live session retains them until the first composing subscription drains the backlog.

Search indexing preserves existing hits and stamps for listed files whose read fails, throttles retries, and replaces them after a successful read; files missing from the supplied list are deleted normally.
Code pieces remove only the separator newline from nonfinal pieces and retain final blank lines, so joining pieces with a newline preserves the original code for first-row copying.

Saved-session loading feeds messages into the transcript incrementally and periodically materializes and pages older settled replies, avoiding the need to hold the entire parsed conversation and all rendered long text in memory at once.

Transcript paging moves the long payload of sufficiently large rows and settled message blocks into process-owned page files while retaining lightweight row metadata; read failures leave the lightweight row in place and page-file creation failures keep content in memory.

The context tally is accumulated message by message, keeps only the latest 300 report rows, and includes an action log that retains the latest 2,000 listed actions while tracking totals and pending tool results.

Markdown export reads the session messages twice: first to associate call IDs with their results and then to stream the rendered document. For file exports, text held behind late tool results spills to a temporary file after a 1 MiB buffer threshold, reducing memory retention without changing message order.

A user-typed `/plugin`, `/plugins`, or `/marketplace` prompt is intercepted by the core session driver and runs Claude Code's plugin command outside the agent loop, in the session's working directory and on its local or remote machine. Successful plugin mutations restart the agent when idle or schedule a restart after the current run so newly installed skills and commands are loaded.

The desktop image viewer decodes on worker threads and uses a bounded full-image cache while a viewer is open; large images may use a screen-sized copy until zoomed, and oversized animations stream frames rather than retaining all frames.

Opening a saved session captures the file length before streaming its history, then reapplies events received during the load over the loaded transcript so current activity is not lost when the older history replaces the initial transcript.

The Claude harness starts a resumed run alongside its history read so prompts can be sent promptly, while history-dependent queries wait for that read; failed or incomplete history reads are surfaced as errors rather than an empty conversation.
The session driver caches each agent's last-listed slash commands by harness kind, remote host, and working directory, allowing a session to offer them before that agent starts.
Desktop shutdown explicitly stops tracked agent process groups: it sends SIGTERM, waits up to about one second, then SIGKILLs remaining groups, including descendants started by those agents.
OpenWiki plan-submission transcript progress remains blank until the streamed arguments contain a pages array, and a completed empty plan is labeled “no pages to change.”
Project settings are issued through Workspace operations, including name, icon and color, and new-session provider configuration is exposed in the per-project settings UI.
Provider settings separate remote-host agent discovery and account status from the shared enabled-agent preference; remote host availability gates the host-specific controls.
ToolCard renders transcript tool results and previews through the session's code-view interface; it is a presentation surface driven by transcript state.
Appearance settings disable glass effects when Qt reports software rendering, retaining the setting for later use rather than trying to draw unsupported blur.
The running workflow card resolves a run for the session and directs pause/resume and stop actions to workspace orchestration by run ID.
